summary: Frontend-only retest (iteration 3) of the 5 fixes from iteration 2 on The Shopkeeper's Day PWA, using Playwright against the public preview URL. ALL 5 previously reported bugs are VERIFIED FIXED: (1) offline page reload keeps the session and renders dashboard/khata/customer-detail from IndexedDB cache with sk_token intact; (2) no duplicate sync - one offline credit of Rs150 + two rapid 'online' events produced exactly ONE ledger entry (balance 2000 -> 2150, 3 transaction rows); (3) offline customer detail and the SellDialog credit-mode customer dropdown both render from cache (dropdown showed 'Ramesh Kumar' while offline, inventory rendered 2 cached products); (4) server-rejected queued item now shows the error toast '1 offline entries were rejected by the server and not saved' instead of a success toast, and the queue drains to 0; (5) digest new_dues_count = 1 distinct customer (Rs2500) and no Radix aria-describedby/DialogTitle console warnings on the Add-Customer or Barcode-Scan dialogs. Seed data verified via API: Ramesh Kumar +919876543210, balance Rs2000 (2500 credit yesterday - 500 payment), digest {yesterday_sales:1240, new_dues:2500, new_dues_count:1, reorder_count:0}. Light regression passed: online credit entry (2150 -> 2249), online cash sell (toast + stock decrement), dashboard digest card values, barcode scanner dialog opens with live camera preview. All test data was cleaned up and Ramesh Kumar's ledger restored to exactly 2 entries / Rs2000 balance; Parle-G stock restored (+1).

minor.issue: A credit ledger entry also inserts a companion doc into the `sales` collection (mode='credit', items=[]). Deleting/cleaning a ledger entry leaves an orphan sales doc that keeps inflating Today's Sales. Observed an orphan credit sale of Rs150 at 22:54 with no matching ledger entry (pre-existing, from an earlier cleanup). Consider linking the sale to the entry id and cascading, or deriving credit revenue from ledger_entries instead of duplicating it.

The companion sales doc created by create_entry does not carry client_id (only ledger_entries does). Idempotency currently works because the ledger dedupe short-circuits before the sale insert, but the sales doc would be untraceable if that order ever changes.

issues: Label pluralisation: renders '1 customers' / '1 txns'. Use singular form when count === 1.

action_items: OPTIONAL (minor): pluralise digest sub-labels ('1 customer' / '1 txn').
OPTIONAL (minor): avoid duplicating credit ledger entries into the `sales` collection, or cascade/link them so cleanup cannot leave orphan revenue rows.
critical_code_review_comments: offline.js flushQueue: module-level `flushing` guard + sequential drain verified correct; `else break` on network error correctly stops the drain and preserves ordering.

AuthContext: token now cleared only on 401/403 and user hydrated from cached 'me' - verified. Note: if the cache is empty (first load on a new device while offline) the user still lands on the login screen; acceptable but worth a friendly offline message instead of the bare login form.

SyncIndicator useEffect depends on [qc, t]; toggling the language re-registers listeners and re-invokes onOnline. Harmless now thanks to the flushing guard, but the effect could be split to avoid needless flush attempts.

All removed; Ramesh Kumar restored to 2 entries / Rs2000 and Parle-G stock restored.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Offline behaviours are testable with page.context.set_offline(True) and page.reload(); the Dexie DB is 'shopkeeper_offline' with object stores 'queue' and 'cache' - you can inspect/inject queue rows via page.evaluate + indexedDB to force sync-failure paths. Customer id for Ramesh Kumar: 8a1b010b-ff81-41dd-993c-6a1ff25a0b7c. Remember credit ledger entries also write a doc into the `sales` collection, so cleanup must delete both. Untested this iteration: real barcode decode (camera preview only), Gemini bill OCR upload, customer OTP portal, suppliers/analytics pages.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A - all iteration-2 defects reproduced as fixed. Duplicate-sync fix confirmed working through both layers: the client-side in-flight guard prevents the second 'online' handler from re-reading the queue, and the server-side client_id idempotency is the backstop.
